statement: Aragon and Navarre were ruled by the same dynasty for much of the 11th–12th centuries. Alfonso I 'the Battler' of Aragon and Navarre (1104–1134) attempted to unite them permanently; his death without heirs split them: Aragon went to Ramon Berenguer IV of Barcelona through marriage; Navarre elected García Ramírez as independent king. Subsequent Navarrese dynasties had French affiliations (Champagne, Évreux). The two kingdoms periodically reunited through dynastic accidents — Ferdinand of Aragon became King of Navarre (1512) by conquest — but were never permanently merged.
